title: Define acceptance checklist and staged gating for latency-corridor enforcement (session-prioritized routing)
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD follow-up: formalize a gated rollout and acceptance criteria for the new session-prioritized routing feature that enforces a latency corridor for interactive chat. The goal is to allow session-prioritized traffic (low-latency sessions) without regressing global tail latency or breaching tenant error budgets. This ticket captures clarified requirements, trade-offs, measurable SLO targets, and an operational checklist to gate each rollout phase.
acceptance_criteria: Define numeric latency corridor targets per workload class: interactive-low (p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 280ms), interactive-medium (p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms)
Global hosted-chat p99 tail must not increase by >10% vs baseline across a 24h baseline window when 25% of traffic is on session-prioritized routing (canary condition)
Per-tenant error-budget consumption attributable to session-prioritized routing must be <= 5% of monthly error budget during staged rollout phases; immediate rollback if >15% in any 30m window
Canary exit criteria: (a) burn-rate <= 1.2 over 1h window AND (b) p99 latency corridor delta <= 10% over same window; otherwise hold or rollback
Observability: dashboards with per-session-class latency histograms, per-tenant burn-rate, and first-byte streaming latency must be available and linked in the runbook
Automated alerts for rapid burn-rate (>=4x baseline) and for p99 tail increase of >25% in 15m windows must be configured and tested
Rollout percentages and cadence defined: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum 2h hold per step and explicit PM/Eng sign-off for progression
Fallback policy: automatic fallback to balanced routing when capacity/latency SLOs are breached; documented in runbook and validated in staging
decisions: Use session-priority as an orthogonal routing key (does not change model variant selection) to limit blast radius
Measure corridor enforcement impact primarily via p99 and burn-rate; p50/p95 for customer experience context
Canary windows: larger windows (1h) for initial small percentages; shortened windows (15-30m) for later ramps because of increased statistical power
Adopt permissive rollout gating in staging to validate instrumentation before production canary
Operational rollback triggers will be automated and reversible (traffic-shift playbooks) rather than requiring manual infra changes
next_steps: ENG: implement per-session metrics (session_class label) and expose in grafana: /d/session-routing/corridor-summary
ENG: add burn-rate attribution for session-prioritized routing in the error budget service (dependency: ENG-18872)
DX/Console: add a rollout control with percentage slider and explicit hold/release buttons (design spec link in attachments)
PM: finalize customer comms and allowed tenant opt-in criteria for early access
SRE: author runbook with automated rollback steps, on-call escalation, and post-mortem template
